title: Lesson 76: Auditing Agents: Logs, Replay, Forensics, and Compliance Evidence
description: How an agent audit record must capture every step of a run, why replay turns that record into a reproducible witness, how digital forensics makes it admissible as evidence, and how the same logs demonstrate compliance.

questions.question: An operator wants to reconstruct what an agent did in production three weeks ago and says she can simply set temperature to zero and re-run the agent to reproduce it. Why is that wrong, per lesson 76?
options: Because temperature only controls the token sampling step, while the logits feeding it vary with batch composition and GPU numerics, so a failing run usually cannot be reproduced by running again, and reproducibility must come from the recorded log
Because temperature zero makes the model refuse to call tools, so the re-run would halt on the first tool call
Because setting temperature to zero disables trace capture, so nothing is recorded on the re-run
Because all cloud inference providers forbid temperature zero for agent workloads
questions.explanation: The lesson explains that temperature controls only the token sampling step; the logits that feed that choice come out of floating point operations that are not bit-identical run to run, influenced by which batch the request lands in and which GPU it hits. OpenAI's seed parameter improves reproducibility without guaranteeing it, and Anthropic notes temperature zero is not fully deterministic. So a failing run usually cannot be reproduced by running again, and deterministic replay instead reconstructs it from the recorded log.

questions.question: A compliance investigator must hand over the trace of a flagged agent run and prove it was not altered since the night it was written. Following lesson 76, what is the correct procedure?
options: Replay the run live against the production system and show the output matches
Recompute the message digest of the exported trace and compare it with the hash recorded at write time, stored out of band, while working from copies and keeping a logged chain of custody
State that the log is on an append-only store and ask that it be trusted
Ask the engineer who restored the agent to confirm nothing was changed
questions.explanation: The lesson applies the NIST SP 800-86 forensic practice of integrity hashing: compute the message digest at collection, store the hash somewhere it cannot be changed, work only on copies, and re-hash to confirm the values still match. A single changed bit produces a completely different digest. The chain of custody, who exported what and when, supports the integrity claim.

questions.question: A company's agent processes personal data and regulators ask it to demonstrate compliance with data-protection principles. Per lesson 76, what role does the agent audit record play?
options: It is optional decoration that carries no regulatory meaning

GDPR Article 5(2) requires the controller to be able to demonstrate compliance, and the unaltered agent trace is that documentation, built in the record-keeping shape that EU AI Act Article 12 requires for high-risk systems
It is useful only for debugging, never for regulators
It replaces the obligation to comply with the underlying rules themselves
questions.explanation: The lesson frames compliance as the ability to demonstrate. GDPR Article 5(2) makes the controller responsible for, and able to demonstrate compliance with, the processing principles, which the ICO frames as keeping evidence of what you did. The EU AI Act's Article 12 requires high-risk systems to allow automatic logging organized around traceability. The unaltered agent trace is the mechanism that makes both demonstrations real.
